name: Slides & Presentations
intro:
Slides and presentations covers AI tools that generate, design, or restructure slide decks from a prompt or outline, rather than tools that merely add AI features to an existing document editor as an afterthought. The boundary here is generation as the primary product: this category excludes general design tools like Canva that happen to offer a presentation mode, and it excludes the AI features Microsoft and Google have bolted onto PowerPoint and Slides, which are add-ons to an existing workflow rather than the product itself. Inside the category sit Gamma, Beautiful.ai, Pitch, Presentations.AI, SlidesAI, Decktopus, and Tome.

A buyer choosing among these is really choosing a workflow. Gamma and Beautiful.ai both build a full deck from a prompt with automated layout, Pitch adds real-time collaboration and is EU-hosted through its German operations, SlidesAI and Decktopus plug directly into Google Slides or offer standalone generation with brand templates, and Presentations.AI targets governed, brand-consistent output for larger teams.

The past year reshaped this market's economics more than its feature set. Gamma disclosed in November 2025 that it had crossed 100 million dollars in annual recurring revenue and raised at a 2.1 billion dollar valuation, evidence that AI-native deck generation has become a durable standalone business rather than a feature people expect from Office or Workspace. At the same time, Tome, one of the category's earliest and most visible entrants, exited the presentation market in late 2025, with its founders relaunching the team as Lightfield, an AI-native CRM, an acknowledgment that consumer-style deck generation alone did not sustain a venture-scale business.

Gamma is now the clearest reference point on revenue and adoption, Pitch is the reference for teams that need EU data residency, and Beautiful.ai remains the reference for design-constrained, brand-locked output.

reading.body:
AI presentation software has consolidated around a small set of vendors, with six of seven tools based in the US, suggesting the category is maturing under American product leadership.

Presentation generation is now a commodity feature across this category. Every tool listed converts input into slide decks through automation. The differentiators are narrow: Decktopus adds data handling capabilities, Pitch.com emphasizes collaboration and EU hosting, Presentations.AI highlights brand governance, and Tome frames its output as narrative design rather than mere layout. These distinctions matter little to the underlying compute requirement, which is modest for this task relative to other AI workloads.

The absence of data about compute intensity, hosting location, or power consumption limits what this category reveals about AI infrastructure. Presentation generation runs on endpoints or cloud instances that need far less power than training or inference for language models. This category does not represent a meaningful load on the electrical grid that constrains AI scaling. It serves instead as a marker of where AI tooling has become routine enough to be packaged as consumer software.
